answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must register identities by committing to a cryptographic stake burning mechanism where the burned deposit scales superlinearly as O(N^2) for N registered identities. In this vast tundra of autonomous nodes, the quadratic friction forces attacker cost to escalate exponentially relative to utility, pushing fraudulent clusters over a financial ledge. Valid entities submit a verifiable stake burn to broadcast an authentic coordinate signal across the network, rendering mass entity replication economically unviable.
